questions.question_text: Translate $A(-4,3)$ $6$ units right. What are the image coordinates?

options.why: Subtracted six, translating left instead of right.
Added six to the vertical coordinate instead of the horizontal coordinate.
Changed the sign of the unchanged vertical coordinate.

questions.question_text: Point $B(1,5)$ is translated to $B'(1,-2)$. Which translation was used?

options.why: Subtracted the coordinate sizes instead of finding the signed change.
Used the correct change on the horizontal direction.
Added the magnitudes five and two but incorrectly removed one when crossing zero.

questions.solution_text:
$-2-5=-7$
The vertical change is $7$ units down.

questions.question_text: Translate $C(3,-5)$ $4$ units left and $8$ units up. What is $C'$?

options.why: Added four, translating right instead of left.
Subtracted eight, translating down instead of up.
Applied the vertical move to $x$ and the horizontal move to $y$.

questions.question_text: Reflect $D(-3,-6)$ in the $x$-axis. What is the image?

options.why: Changed the sign of $x$, reflecting in the $y$-axis instead.
Changed both coordinate signs instead of only $y$.
Swapped the coordinates instead of reflecting across an axis.

questions.question_text: Reflect $E(7,-2)$ in the $y$-axis. What is the image?

options.why: Changed the sign of $y$, reflecting in the $x$-axis instead.
Changed both signs instead of keeping $y$ unchanged.
Swapped the coordinates instead of changing the sign of $x$.

questions.question_text:
The diagram shows $P$ and its reflected image $P'$. Which axis is the mirror line?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.68]
\draw[gray!30,very thin](-4,-4)grid(4,4);\draw[<->](-4.5,0)--(4.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[<->](0,-4.5)--(0,4.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(-2,3)circle(2.5pt)node[above left]{$P$};\fill(-2,-3)circle(2.5pt)node[below left]{$P'$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: That mirror line would change the sign of $x$, not the sign of $y$.
Missed that the points have equal distances on opposite sides of the $x$-axis.

questions.solution_text:
$x=-2$ stays fixed and $y$ changes from $3$ to $-3$.
The transformation is reflection in the $x$-axis.
